routes.description: Establish that a personal creator and revelation provide a unified explanation for the universe’s existence and order, biological information, objective morality and reason, and historically grounded supernatural disclosure.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cited features of reality require or are best unified by a transcendent personal cause, atheistic naturalism lacks comparable foundations for them, and evidence independently bridges generic theism to credible revelation.

motionBridge.description: Show that personal-creator theism with revelation explains the principal features of reality more adequately than a reality containing no supernatural dimension.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the finite physical universe requires an eternal, nonphysical, purposive cause capable of initiating spacetime.
Connect life-permitting cosmic conditions and biological information to intelligence rather than unguided natural processes.
Ground objective moral obligation, truth, logic, rational cognition, and scientific intelligibility in a transcendent mind.
Supply independent historical and epistemic grounds for moving from generic creator theism to personal action and credible revelation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that cosmic decay, suffering, and religious wrongdoing do not by themselves defeat purposeful creation or the truth of theism.
Require the atheistic alternative to account positively for the same cosmological, biological, moral, and rational data.

routes.description: Establish that natural processes and human social, psychological, and historical development explain the relevant features of reality without a supernatural hypothesis, while creator and revelation claims introduce unsupported inferences and additional difficulties.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts remain sufficient without complete ultimate knowledge, the move from physical origins to a personal revealed deity is unwarranted, and observed suffering, religious diversity, and unreliable miracle traditions favor human and natural explanations.

motionBridge.description: Show that no supernatural dimension is needed to explain reality and that adding a personal creator and revelation yields no superior comparative explanation.

centralBridges.description: Separate scientific uncertainty about ultimate origins from evidence for a creator and show that physical explanations do not require a divine assumption.
Explain apparent biological design and human experience through evolution, physical processes, and other natural mechanisms.
Account for moral knowledge and responsibility through human solidarity, law, and social life without supernatural command or enforcement.
Explain religions and revelation claims as diverse human products while challenging miracle testimony and exclusive doctrinal authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test claims of competent benevolent design against cosmic waste, extinction, disease, prolonged suffering, and delayed revelation.
Assess whether doctrines of unaccountable divine authority generate coercion or violence rather than necessary moral guidance.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin and the Necessity of a Creator
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether the universe’s finite existence requires a personal transcendent cause or whether physical explanation can remain adequate while ultimate origins are uncertain.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Biological Information, and Natural Order
sections.rationale: This section tests the competing explanatory inferences from life-permitting conditions and biological complexity to intelligence, evolution, or other unguided natural processes.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Authority, and Human Solidarity
sections.rationale: The clash determines whether objective obligation requires a divine standard or whether moral knowledge, responsibility, and criticism can be grounded in human social existence.

sections.title: Reason, Truth, and Experience under Naturalism
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether logic, rational cognition, science, love, and transcendence require an immaterial theistic foundation or remain intelligible within naturalism.

sections.title: Revelation, Miracles, and the Human Origins of Religion
sections.rationale: This section governs the necessary bridge from generic creator claims to personal revelation by testing miracle evidence, scriptural reliability, religious diversity, and naturalistic accounts of belief.

routes.description: Establish that consciousness, intentionality, agency, and personal identity cannot be exhausted by physical descriptions, then identify a single nonphysical subject capable of persisting independently of its present body and entering later embodiment.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the mental features and identity conditions require a nonphysical bearer, bodily dependence is compatible with that bearer's continued existence, and a coherent mechanism or argument supports survival beyond bodily death.

motionBridge.description: Show that a conscious person includes one nonphysical subject whose identity can continue after the present organism dies.

centralBridges.description: Establish that phenomenal character or intrinsic intentionality is not captured by an exclusively physical inventory.
Connect irreducible mental properties to a single subject that bears and unifies the person's mental states.
Supply identity conditions under which that subject can remain the same person across bodily discontinuity or renewed embodiment.
Explain why dependence of embodied capacities on the brain does not entail destruction of the subject when the brain ceases functioning.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use reason-responsive agency or freedom to reinforce the distinction between mentality and bottom-up physical causation.
Provide cosmological or probabilistic support for recurrence or another opportunity for postmortem embodiment.

routes.description: Account for consciousness, intentionality, agency, and personal unity as properties or activities of natural organisms at appropriate explanatory scales, while challenging any inference from mental distinctiveness to a separable enduring substance.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic organism-level explanations accommodate the cited mental phenomena, brain dependence undermines an independently functioning bearer, and the proposed identity or cosmological grounds for postmortem survival are not required.

motionBridge.description: Show that the conscious person is a natural organism and that no independently surviving nonphysical subject is needed.

centralBridges.description: Explain mental properties at the organismic scale without reducing them to microphysical vocabulary or adding another substance.
Give physicalist-compatible accounts of phenomenal knowledge, intentional attitudes, and unified consciousness.
Use the systematic dependence of mental capacities on brain states and integrity to oppose separable personal existence.
Challenge the identity conditions and cosmological premises offered to support recurrence or postmortem persistence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve deliberation and reason-responsive action through compatibilist or higher-scale causal explanation.
Relate the onset and loss of conscious capacities to the presence of suitable neural organization.

sections.title: Phenomenal consciousness and physical explanation

sections.rationale: Competing accounts of aboutness, reason-responsive action, and higher-level causation test whether mental activity requires a nonphysical source or fits an organismic framework.

sections.title: From nonphysical properties to subjects and personal identity
sections.rationale: The motion concerns substances rather than merely unusual properties, making the inference to a unified subject and its criteria of persistence an indispensable burden.

sections.title: Cosmology, recurrence, and postmortem survival
sections.rationale: The temporal probability argument, recurrence mechanism, and rival cosmological models bear on whether personal existence can recur after bodily death.

sections.title: Brain dependence, embodiment, and disembodied capacity
sections.rationale: Evidence concerning brain impairment, suitable neural conditions, and the capacities of a disembodied subject bears directly on separability and survival.

routes.description: Establish a defensible prior framework, support the principal historical data through reliable testimony, and show that their conjunction is more expected if Jesus rose than under the relevant competing explanations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the historical sources warrant the central burial, empty-tomb, appearance, and witness data, the resurrection hypothesis has a non-prohibitive prior, and its comparative likelihood for the combined data exceeds the alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect the supported historical data and prior considerations to the conclusion that resurrection is more probable than the competing hypotheses.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the relevant texts and testimonial traditions provide sufficiently reliable access to the claimed historical events.
Establish the death and burial, empty tomb, reported appearances, conversions, and costly witness conduct as data requiring comparative explanation.
Show that mistake, hallucination, fabrication, continued burial, and comparable rival accounts predict the combined data less well than resurrection.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply background reasons concerning divine agency and incarnation that prevent the resurrection prior from being evidentially insurmountable.
Support the durability and sincerity of the reported experiences while distinguishing those properties from the final historical inference.

routes.description: Apply demanding but claim-sensitive historical standards, challenge the reliability and independence of the proposed data, and deny that comparative or Bayesian framing can supply warrant absent adequate support for the event itself.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the claimed death, tomb, appearances, or transmission remain insufficiently established, or if the inference from those reports to resurrection fails to exceed natural alternatives and rational uncertainty remains available.

motionBridge.description: Connect deficiencies in the data and inference to the conclusion that the historical evidence does not make resurrection more probable than competing hypotheses.

centralBridges.description: Require source proximity, independence, corroboration, confirmed witnesses, and evidence proportionate to the extraordinary character of the claim.
Challenge whether death, burial, an empty tomb, appearances, and accurate transmission are independently established historical data.
Distinguish reports, sincerity, transformation, and expected evidence under resurrection from evidence that resurrection actually occurred.
Preserve an unknown or unconvinced conclusion when exhaustive hypotheses lack sufficiently grounded probability assignments.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate whether the event occurred from claims about God, supernatural mechanisms, present miracles, or other alleged returns from death.
Test whether selective disclosure, obscure testimony, and sacrificial means fit the divine background assumptions used to support the prior.

sections.title: Probability Method, Priors, and Rational Uncertainty
sections.rationale: This issue governs how the historical material may update an initial probability, whether qualitative likelihoods are usable, and whether the largest member of an exhaustive set warrants belief or leaves uncertainty.

sections.title: Source Reliability, Independence, and Transmission
sections.rationale: The resurrection comparison depends on whether the New Testament writings and underlying testimony provide sufficiently early, independent, corroborated, and accurately transmitted access to the alleged events.

sections.title: Death, Burial, and Empty-Tomb Foundations
sections.rationale: Death, placement in a known tomb, and subsequent emptiness form a central evidential sequence, while disputes over confirmation determine whether that sequence is available for explanation at all.

sections.title: Appearances, Memory, Sincerity, and Transformation
sections.rationale: Reported encounters and witness conduct supply a principal affirmative datum, but their force depends on memory, identification, sincerity, transmission, and the distinction between committed belief and truth.

sections.title: Competing Explanations and Supernatural Context
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing resurrection with mistake, hallucination, fabrication, and other explanations while determining whether divine agency, incarnation, modern miracles, or analogous claims legitimately affect that comparison.

routes.description: Establish that Iraq's exceptional conduct made intervention defensible despite its costs, while showing that morality and political judgment do not require divine authority and can be corrupted by religious command, institutions, or absolutism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by supplying a principled basis for overriding Iraqi sovereignty, connecting removal to defensible ends, grounding moral agency independently of revelation, and explaining how asserted divine authority can distort conduct or obstruct peaceful political settlement.

motionBridge.description: Show both that intervention in Iraq met a defensible exception to restraint and that religion can corrupt rather than uniquely supply moral authority.

centralBridges.description: Identify regime conduct serious enough to defeat the ordinary presumption of sovereignty and nonintervention.
Connect regime removal and post-invasion consequences to humanitarian or strategic ends capable of answering foreseeable costs.
Explain how truth, solidarity, and moral responsibility can operate without commands from a personal deity.
Show mechanisms by which divine authorization, absolutism, or religious institutions can license harm or impede revisable judgment.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Challenge the evidentiary passage from cosmic origins or order to a personal, morally authoritative deity.
Distinguish harms caused by secular humanism from harms merely committed by regimes carrying atheist or anti-clerical labels.

routes.description: Establish that the Iraq invasion lacked a coherent justification sufficient to overcome its foreseeable human and strategic costs, while showing that transcendent authority grounds objective moral obligation and that religion's abuses do not negate its moral and civilizational functions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by maintaining the moral distinction between aggression and restraint, demonstrating an adverse or inconsistent intervention rationale, explaining why secular preference cannot bind moral duty, and answering claims that religious belief uniquely causes cruelty or tyranny.

motionBridge.description: Show both that the Iraq invasion failed the burden for justified war and that religion can supply indispensable moral authority despite misuse.

centralBridges.description: Require a coherent and sufficiently exceptional justification before aggressive war may override sovereignty and the presumption of restraint.
Account for civilian, military, fiscal, strategic, and moral consequences when testing whether intervention was defensible.
Explain why recognition of moral rules requires an authority beyond individual or collective preference to become binding.
Show how religious belief can redirect destructive impulses, support self-government, and sustain moral or civilizational order despite human misuse.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend contested religious narratives by distinguishing their governing lesson from the harmful act represented within them.
Use avowedly anti-religious persecution to test claims that removing religious authority reliably prevents absolutism or political cruelty.

sections.title: Sovereignty, Aggression, and the Case for Intervention
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether Saddam Hussein's conduct created a principled exception to sovereignty and whether intervention and nonintervention bear materially different moral burdens.

sections.title: Consequences and Strategic Balance in Iraq
sections.rationale: The defensibility of intervention also turns on its anticipated and realized human, fiscal, regional, humanitarian, and institutional consequences.

sections.title: From Cosmic Order to Divine Moral Authority
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether arguments from origin, order, or design warrant belief in a personal deity capable of grounding authoritative moral requirements.

sections.title: Secular Moral Agency and Transcendent Obligation
sections.rationale: The central moral-authority clash concerns whether solidarity and reason can ground responsible conduct or whether binding obligation requires a transcendent source.

sections.title: Religious Command, Redemption, and Practical Harm
sections.rationale: Contested doctrines and examples reveal whether religious authority restrains destructive impulses or instead licenses submission, transferred guilt, absolutism, and political obstruction.

sections.title: Religion, Atheism, and Political Tyranny
sections.rationale: Historical disputes over fascist, communist, clerical, and anti-clerical power test the claimed causal relationship between religious or secular commitments and organized persecution.

routes.description: Establish that necessary truths are propositions requiring an ontological ground, that propositions are intrinsically intentional and best understood as thoughts, and that their objectivity and necessity require an eternal divine mind rather than human minds or mind-independent abstract objects.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by securing proposition realism, connecting propositional intentionality to mentality, showing that a necessary divine mind can ground objective and necessary propositions, and establishing an explanatory advantage over Platonism and other alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect the existence and character of necessary propositions to their grounding as thoughts in a necessarily existing divine mind.

centralBridges.description: Establish that necessary truths involve real propositions rather than merely linguistic, physical, or human constructions.
Show that the intrinsic aboutness and aspectual character of propositions are best explained by treating propositions as thoughts.
Show that divine thoughts can supply propositions with necessary existence, objectivity, and shareability without depending on contingent human cognition.
Demonstrate that divine conceptualism explains intentionality and causal relevance more fully than mind-independent Platonism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify at least one unavoidable truth without requiring certainty about any particular classical logical law or a complete theory of modality.
Explain how divine thoughts can constitute propositional contents without generating a distinctive content regress or self-reference problem.

motionBridge.description: Show that necessary propositions admit a coherent non-divine explanation, so their existence does not require a necessarily existing divine mind.

centralBridges.description: Establish that propositions may possess intentionality without being mental and that the contrary inference needs independent support.
Show that mind-independent propositions can account for objective, shareable, and necessarily true contents.
Test whether identifying propositions with divine thoughts yields determinate content without regress, relabeling, or an unstable thought-content distinction.
Show that divine conceptualism does not gain an explanatory or ontological advantage merely by redescribing abstract propositions as divine thoughts.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish logical, epistemic, and metaphysical necessity and require adequate support for claims about unavoidable truths.
Separate objections common to proposition realism from considerations that genuinely discriminate between divine conceptualism and Platonism.

routes.description: Establish that naturalism has greater intrinsic probability and that physical reality, biological history, embodied mentality, suffering, moral handicaps, and nonresistant nonbelief are collectively more expected on naturalism than on theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by defending the comparative-probability method, showing that the cited evidence supplies independent or cumulative support for naturalism, and answering theistic appeals to creation, fine-tuning, information, reason, morality, and science.

motionBridge.description: Connect naturalism's intrinsic plausibility and total comparative evidential fit to the conclusion that it better explains reality than theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish a defensible intrinsic-probability advantage for naturalism through modesty and coherence without assuming the evidential conclusion.
Show that physical reality, evolution, embodied minds, suffering, moral handicaps, and hiddenness have greater expectedness on naturalism.
Show that creation, fine-tuning, biological information, reason, morality, and scientific order do not yield a superior theistic explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish causal naturalism from scientism and from denial of every abstract, acausal, or nonphysical reality.
Preserve comparative inference by addressing alternative hypotheses, evidential dependencies, and the limits of claims based on unresolved phenomena.

routes.description: Establish that a prior intelligent personal agent better accounts for cosmic creation and sustenance, fine-tuning, biological information, rational thought, objective morality, natural order, evil, and the foundations of science than naturalism does.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by supporting the principal theistic inferences, showing that their explanatory domains form a cumulative case, and answering naturalistic objections from simplicity, evolution, embodied minds, suffering, hiddenness, and moral disagreement.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory case for an intelligent personal ground to the conclusion that theism better explains reality than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that cosmic origin or contingency, fine-tuning, biological information, and natural directedness support an intelligent transcendent cause.
Establish that rational agency, logical and mathematical order, and objective moral obligation require grounding unavailable to naturalism.
Show that physical determination and exclusively natural causes leave material explanatory commitments unsupported or internally unstable.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply theistic accounts of suffering, nonresistant nonbelief, evolution, and moral disagreement sufficient to resist their proposed evidential force.
Explain how divine grounding and intelligent causation can complement scientific accounts of regular operation and inquiry.

sections.title: Worldview Scope, Intrinsic Probability, and Comparative Method
sections.rationale: The motion depends on how naturalism and theism are defined, how modesty and coherence affect prior probability, and how evidence and alternative explanations are combined without invalid inference.

sections.title: Cosmic Existence, Contingency, Order, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: Physical reality, cosmic origin and sustenance, life-permitting conditions, and natural regularity form a principal clash over whether reality points to natural necessity or transcendent agency.

sections.title: Evolution, Biological Information, and Life's History
sections.rationale: Evolutionary evidence, fossil history, genetic information, and proposed natural origins of life test the competing expectations and explanatory resources of both worldviews.

sections.title: Embodied Mind, Rational Reliability, and Scientific Knowledge
sections.rationale: Mind-brain dependence, determinism, evolved cognition, logical and mathematical order, and the presuppositions of science bear directly on whether either worldview can account for reliable reasoning.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Suffering, and Moral Agency
sections.rationale: Moral grounding, pain, allegedly gratuitous evil, neurological moral handicaps, freedom, and moral disagreement jointly test each worldview's account of value and morally significant experience.

sections.title: Divine Hiddenness and Overall Explanatory Balance
sections.rationale: Nonresistant nonbelief and proposed reasons for divine silence create a direct relational test of theism, while the final cumulative comparison connects all evidential domains to the motion.

routes.description: Build a cumulative historical inference from early resurrection testimony, the unexpected individual-resurrection claim, Christianity's worldwide expansion, and later cross-cultural visions to Jesus's historical resurrection.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the relevant phenomena are historically supported, resist the principal ordinary and comparative explanations, and jointly make an actual resurrection a plausible explanation of the motion's full evidential pattern.

motionBridge.description: Show why the combined pattern of early appearances, unexpected messianic interpretation, worldwide expansion, and later visions points to Jesus actually rising from the dead.

centralBridges.description: Establish that early and multiple appearance testimony provides historically significant support for encounters with the risen Jesus.
Show that available Jewish expectations do not adequately explain the emergence of the claim that one crucified Messiah had already bodily risen.
Connect Christianity's exceptional expansion and fulfillment of Jesus's stated worldwide mission to the continuing activity of the risen Jesus.
Show that recurring visions of Jesus, especially among non-Christians who convert, are distinctive evidence of continuing risen activity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify relevant differences between the resurrection evidence and allegedly comparable testimony from other religious traditions.
Explain why each evidential line contributes as part of a cumulative case even if no single line independently establishes resurrection.

routes.description: Show that critical historical inquiry cannot infer a physical resurrection from indirect appearance reports, psychologically and socially explicable belief formation, religious growth, or recurring vision traditions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the offered phenomena remain compatible with ordinary testimonial, perceptual, psychological, social, or comparative religious explanations, leaving resurrection insufficiently established as a historical conclusion.

motionBridge.description: Show that the admissible historical evidence does not overcome ordinary explanations or the probability problem posed by an otherwise unprecedented return from death.

centralBridges.description: Establish that most named appearance claims are indirectly reported and must be tested by the same reliability standards applied to comparable religious testimony.
Explain how perceived postmortem experiences, prior knowledge, psychology, Jewish afterlife concepts, and social reinforcement could generate resurrection belief.
Show that Christianity's influence and expansion demonstrate conviction or institutional success without identifying a miraculous historical cause.
Show that dreams and later visions neither establish the reality of their objects nor uniquely distinguish Christianity from other religious traditions.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use structurally comparable witness, miracle, growth, and vision traditions to test whether the affirmative applies its evidential criteria impartially.
Maintain the distinction between theological interpretation and the source criticism and probability judgments required for a historical conclusion.

sections.title: Early Appearance Testimony and Source Reliability
sections.rationale: This issue tests the historical basis of the earliest appearance claims, including direct versus indirect testimony, multiplicity, accessibility, and consistent treatment of comparable religious witnesses.

sections.title: Unexpected Messianic Claim and Formation of Resurrection Belief
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether an individual risen Messiah was too unexpected to arise naturally or could emerge from visionary experiences, Jewish afterlife concepts, and communal reinforcement.

sections.title: Ordinary Explanations and Historical Probability
sections.rationale: This issue examines bereavement experiences, mistaken perception, Paul's conversion, cumulative inference, physical regularities, and the evidential standard for establishing resurrection historically.

sections.title: Christianity's Expansion, Influence, and Fulfilled Mission
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether Christianity's worldwide growth and Jesus's exceptional influence support continuing risen activity or merely record the later success of a religious movement.

sections.title: Later Visions and Comparative Religious Experience
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether cross-cultural visions of Jesus provide distinctive continuing evidence or remain nondiagnostic alongside dreams, healings, and vision traditions found in other religions.

routes.description: Establish that contingent reality requires an explanation outside the totality of contingent things, that this explanatory foundation exists necessarily, and that its comparative explanatory virtues support identifying it as God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if contingency remains distinct from causal determination, the explanatory principle applies to the plurality of contingent things without an illicit composition inference, and a perfect necessary being is supported over a necessary-universe terminus.

motionBridge.description: Connect the necessary foundation of contingent reality to God through a warranted deductive or abductive identification.

centralBridges.description: Establish that reality includes genuinely contingent things whose existence calls for explanation despite any deterministic causal history.
Show that explaining contingent things individually or through their plurality does not remove the need for a non-contingent explanatory foundation.
Show that simplicity, absence of arbitrary limits, or cumulative theistic considerations favor a perfect necessary being over a necessary universe.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify the relationship between modal contingency, existential dependence, causal determination, and explanatory need.
Ground the demand for explanation in ordinary inquiry, scientific practice, induction, or the stable order of reality.

routes.description: Block the theistic contingency inference by challenging the establishment of genuine contingency, the move from contingent members to an external foundation, and the identification of any necessary reality as God rather than the universe.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if determinism or a necessary-universe option remains viable, if the totality-level explanatory demand is unsupported, or if the proposed divine terminus lacks a non-question-begging advantage over non-theistic necessary reality.

motionBridge.description: Show that the argument does not establish a distinct necessary foundation with attributes sufficient for identification as God.

centralBridges.description: Require justification that observed things could have existed differently and test whether determinism transmits necessity through the causal order.
Show that moving from explanations of contingent members to an explanation outside their totality may assume composition or explanatory convergence.
Preserve a necessary or brute universe as an alternative explanatory terminus and test whether it is at least as simple as a divine foundation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require a principled distinction between treating God as necessarily self-explanatory and allowing comparable treatment of non-divine reality.
Examine whether perfection, unlimited power, divine will, or theological complexity supports rather than undermines the claimed identification.

sections.title: Contingency, Determinism, and Necessity
sections.rationale: The first-stage argument depends on whether anything is genuinely contingent and whether causal determination differs from metaphysical necessity or instead transmits necessity through the causal chain.

sections.title: Explanatory Principle and Legitimate Stopping Points
sections.rationale: The competing burdens require determining why contingent existence calls for explanation and whether explanatory termination at God is principled when analogous termination at non-divine reality is proposed.

sections.title: Plurality, Composition, and External Explanation
sections.rationale: The central transition from explanations of individual contingent things to an explanation beyond their totality turns on composition, plurality, regress, convergence, and possible circularity concerns.

sections.title: Necessary Being or Necessary Universe
sections.rationale: Even if some necessary reality is granted, the motion requires comparison between a distinct necessary being and the option that the universe or lawful reality is itself necessary or brute.

sections.title: Identification with God and Explanatory Virtues
sections.rationale: The final motion-level inference requires grounds for divine attributes and tests whether perfection, simplicity, absence of arbitrary limits, and cumulative theistic considerations distinguish God from rival foundations.

routes.description: Establish the cluelessness thesis by showing that current origin-of-life research lacks an experimentally verified, prebiotically realistic pathway from chemical precursors to a functional and evolvable living system.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the absence of adequate mechanisms for selective biomolecule formation, functional information, replication, persistence, and integrated cellular organization warrants describing present knowledge as unable to explain life's chemical origin.

motionBridge.description: Show that presently available research does not supply a valid and experimentally supported hypothesis that satisfies the essential chemical and systems requirements for originating life.

centralBridges.description: Show that proposed prebiotic processes do not reliably produce sufficiently long, stable, selectively linked, and biologically relevant polymers from realistic mixtures and conditions.
Show that current accounts neither generate the first functional informational polymer nor establish replication and evolution without presupposing organized catalysts or templates.
Show that isolated chemical results have not been joined into a continuous pathway that supplies compatible compartments, energy, coding, replication, and functional organization.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether cited demonstrations depend on purified materials, activation steps, solvents, catalysts, or environmental arrangements that lack adequate prebiotic justification.
Maintain that acknowledging a missing scientific mechanism is a present-tense epistemic conclusion and does not itself imply a supernatural cause.

routes.description: Reject the cluelessness thesis by showing that prebiotic chemistry, ribozyme research, mineral and environmental mechanisms, and systems chemistry provide experimentally grounded and progressively connectable pathways toward abiogenesis.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if current research offers testable mechanisms for multiple essential transitions and a viable gradual framework toward protocells, even though no unique historical sequence or complete modern cell has been reconstructed.

motionBridge.description: Show that experimentally supported mechanisms and viable research pathways constitute substantive knowledge, so incompleteness or uncertainty among alternatives does not amount to cluelessness.

centralBridges.description: Establish plausible experimental routes for forming, concentrating, polymerizing, enriching, protecting, and encapsulating relevant biomolecules in prebiotic analog environments.
Establish that mixed-linkage functional RNA, catalytic ribozymes, cooperative replicators, and selection research provide mechanisms for heredity and progressive complexity.
Establish that systems chemistry can couple replicators, vesicles, environmental cycling, and selection gradually without requiring the spontaneous assembly of a modern cell.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that mechanisms such as mineral stabilization, functional tolerance, restricted early alphabets, and chiral enrichment materially mitigate alleged chemical barriers.
Test whether criticisms of experimental controls, analytical results, literature claims, and model conditions accurately characterize what the cited research demonstrates.

sections.title: Meaning and Evidentiary Standard of Cluelessness
sections.rationale: The motion depends on whether knowledge requires a complete experimentally verified origin sequence or whether tested partial mechanisms and viable pathways suffice despite historical uncertainty.

sections.title: Prebiotic Synthesis, Selectivity, and Environmental Plausibility
sections.rationale: The feasibility of producing peptides, nucleotides, sugars, polymers, and chiral enrichment under relevant conditions is a principal clash over whether laboratory progress bears on early Earth.

sections.title: RNA Function, Replication, and Biological Information
sections.rationale: Linkage selectivity, catalytic function, the first replicator, copying capacity, functional sequence, and selection form the central disputed bridge from nonliving chemistry to heredity and evolution.

sections.title: Polymer Stability, Mineral Surfaces, and Reaction Compatibility
sections.rationale: A viable pathway must reconcile polymer degradation with proposed stabilization and determine whether preservation mechanisms remain compatible with the reactions needed for further chemical development.

sections.title: Systems Integration and Gradual Protocell Pathways
sections.rationale: The ultimate burden concerns whether separate advances can be coupled into compartments, replication, energy use, growth, and selection without presupposing the integrated organization being explained.

sections.title: Scientific Interpretation and Epistemic Scope
sections.rationale: Disputes over literature interpretation, expertise, public presentation, and supernatural inference bear on the reliability and proper scope of the competing claims without replacing the chemical issues.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve a causal or realizing role for consciousness against zombie-based and empirical-inertness objections.
Address compatibility with established physics and the challenge of combining simple conscious entities into unified subjects.

routes.description: Defend consciousness as a real higher-level feature instantiated by physical organization, specify a multilevel empirical explanation connecting brain states, experience, behavior, and dynamics, and show why adding fundamental consciousness does not improve on the constrained physical account.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if higher-level physical description can account for conscious experience without new fundamental ontology and if consciousness-first alternatives either conflict with established physical constraints or fail to add explanatory and causal consequences.

motionBridge.description: Connect weak emergence and multilevel physical explanation to a complete account of consciousness that requires no additional fundamental conscious entities.

centralBridges.description: Establish that conscious concepts can be valid higher-level descriptions of systems wholly constituted by physical processes.
Specify how mappings among physical states, experience, behavior, and dynamics could constitute an explanation of consciousness.
Use the tested physical account of human-scale interactions to constrain proposals that add or alter fundamental ontology.
Require a consciousness-first theory either to identify consequential changes to physics or explain what unchanged fundamental consciousness adds.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that private qualitative evidence can be included within broad empirical inquiry without establishing nonphysical fundamentals.
Relate consciousness to physical organization and behavior while addressing zombie and causal-irrelevance arguments.

sections.title: Qualitative Experience and the Scope of Physical Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue tests the central physicalist burden: whether quantitative neural descriptions and multilevel mappings can explain what experience is like, including the knowledge argument and the claimed explanatory gap.

sections.title: Emergence versus Consciousness-First Grounding
sections.rationale: This issue compares the rival motion-level accounts: consciousness as a higher-level physical description and consciousness as the intrinsic basis that realizes physical structure.

sections.title: Empirical Constraints and Theoretical Consequences
sections.rationale: This issue determines how each ontology relates to established physics and whether preserving or changing physical dynamics supplies explanatory, causal, or testable consequences.

sections.title: First-Person Data and the Method of Inquiry
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether private conscious awareness requires philosophical synthesis beyond physical science or can be incorporated within an appropriately broad empirical method.

sections.title: Causation, Zombies, and the Unity of Consciousness
sections.rationale: This issue covers supporting burdens concerning consciousness's role in behavior, the implications of physically identical duplicates, multiple realization, and the formation of unified subjects from simpler conscious bases.
